post.description: Creates an unverified account and issues a verification challenge by email. No application data is reachable until verification completes.

201.description: The account was created and a verification email was queued.

400.description: The password does not meet the policy, or the address is malformed.

409.description: The address already holds an account.

post.summary: Register an account with an email address and a password

post.description: Consumes the single-use token from the verification link and activates the account. The token is sent in the body rather than followed as a link so that a mail scanner opening the URL cannot consume it.

400.description: The link is not valid — never issued, already used, expired, or belonging to an account that has itself expired. The four are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.summary: Verify control of a registered email address

post.description: Sends a fresh confirmation link if the address holds an unverified account, and does nothing otherwise. The response is identical in every case, so it cannot be used to discover whether an address is registered.

202.description: Accepted. Empty by design — a body describing what happened would be the disclosure this endpoint exists without.

400.description: The address is malformed. A statement about the request, not about whether an account exists.

post.summary: Request a new verification link

post.description: Sends a single-use, time-limited reset link if the address holds a verified account, and does nothing otherwise. The response is identical in every case. Requests are rate-limited per address; a locked account may always request one — consuming the link is what releases the lock.

202.description: Accepted. Empty by design, for the same reason as the verification resend: a body describing what happened would be the disclosure this endpoint exists without.

400.description: The address is malformed. A statement about the request, not about accounts.

429.description: Too many requests for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Request a password reset link

post.description: Consumes the single-use token and replaces the password. Every existing session for the account is terminated, and a lockout, if one stood, is released. The token is sent in the body rather than followed as a link so a mail scanner cannot consume it. No session is issued: sign in with the new password.

204.description: The password is replaced. Sign in to continue.

400.description: The password does not meet the policy, or the link is not valid — never issued, already used, expired, or superseded by a newer request. The four are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset link

get.description: What S-28 reads. It carries neither the secret nor the codes: both exist outside the user’s own keeping only at the moment they are issued.
get.summary: Whether this account has a second factor, and how many recovery codes remain

post.description: Issues a secret for the authenticator to capture. **The factor is not yet in force** — it activates only when a current code confirms the capture, because a secret an authenticator failed to record would otherwise leave the account demanding a code no device can produce. Requires the current password, since a second factor is the control that survives a compromised session and a compromised session must not be able to install one.

201.description: The secret and its enrolment URI, returned exactly once.

403.description: The current password did not match (problem type credential-invalid).

409.description: A confirmed factor already exists; turn it off before enrolling another.

post.summary: Begin enrolling a second factor

post.description: Activates the factor and issues the recovery codes, which are shown exactly once. No password here: the enrolment step took it moments ago, and a current code from the secret just issued is stronger evidence than a password for the thing being proved.

201.description: The factor is in force, and these are its recovery codes.

403.description: The code is not current for the issued secret (problem type factor-invalid).

409.description: There is no enrolment awaiting confirmation.

post.summary: Confirm the enrolment with a current code, and receive the recovery codes

post.description: Removes the factor and its recovery codes together — a code left behind would sign in against a factor that no longer exists. Requires the current password. NFR-95 is opt-in, and an opt-in that cannot be reversed is not one.

204.description: The factor and its recovery codes are gone.

403.description: The current password did not match (problem type credential-invalid).

409.description: The account has no second factor.

post.summary: Turn the second factor off

post.description: Replaces the whole set rather than topping it up, so a user who re-issues because they believe a code leaked does not leave the leaked one live. Requires the current password.

201.description: The new set. Every previous code is now dead.

403.description: The current password did not match (problem type credential-invalid).

409.description: The account has no confirmed second factor.

post.summary: Replace the recovery codes with a fresh set

post.description: Requires the current password (FR-7). Optionally ends the account’s **other** active sessions — the one making the request is spared, so the device the change was made from keeps working. A provider-only account has no password to change and is refused; setting a first password for one is FR-8’s path.

200.description: The password was replaced, with a count of the other sessions ended.

400.description: The new password does not meet the policy.

403.description: The current password is not right, or the account holds none (problem type credential-invalid). Deliberately one answer for both.

429.description: Too many re-authentication attempts for this account in the window (§12.5.6). It bounds the route without touching FR-4’s lockout, so a mistype here cannot sign the user out.

post.summary: Change the signed-in account’s password

post.description: Verifies the credential and issues a session: a short-lived access token and a single-use refresh token. Failures are uniform for unknown addresses and wrong passwords alike, rate-limited per address, and locked out after repeated failure.

201.description: Two shapes, discriminated by `kind`. `signed_in` carries the session — the answer for an account with no second factor, which is most of them (NFR-95 is opt-in). `challenged` means the credential was correct and the account has a second factor, so a challenge is returned instead of a session (UC-194); complete it at `POST /auth/session/factor`. Branch on `kind`, never on the presence of a field.

401.description: The email address or the password is not right. Deliberately one answer for both, and for a wrong password on an unverified account.

403.description: The credential is valid but cannot sign in: the address is not verified yet (problem type email-unverified), or the account is locked after repeated failures (problem type account-locked, released by password reset).

429.description: Too many attempts for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Sign in with an email address and a password

delete.description: Terminates the session server-side: the refresh token is dead from here on, whatever copies of it exist. Idempotent, and identical for tokens that were never real — signing out is not an endpoint that confirms anything. Signing out of the platform does not end any session at a social identity provider.

204.description: The session is terminated, or already was.

post.description: The second step for an account with a second factor enrolled (UC-194, UC-195). Present the challenge from the first step together with a current code from the authenticator — or one of the account’s recovery codes, in the same field, since the two formats cannot be confused. The challenge lives five minutes and is deliberately **not** single-use: a mistyped code leaves the caller on this step to retype, rather than back at the password.

201.description: The factor was answered and the session issued.

403.description: The code is not right, or the challenge has expired or was not issued by this API (problem type factor-invalid). Deliberately one answer for all three: the distinctions describe our verification to whoever is probing it and none changes what to do next. Also the account being locked after repeated failures (problem type account-locked) — distinct because reaching it takes ten consecutive failures against a real credential, so it discloses nothing to anyone who has not already done that, and the way out is the reset link rather than another code.

429.description: Too many attempts for this account in the window.

post.summary: Complete a sign-in that requires a second factor

post.description: Rotates the session: the presented refresh token is consumed and a successor pair issued. Presenting an already-consumed token is refused; the session stays bounded by its idle and absolute lifetimes.

401.description: The token is not usable (problem type authentication-required), or the session has reached a lifetime bound (problem type session-expired) — the latter is the signal to re-authenticate in place with work preserved.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a fresh token pair

get.description: The set the sign-in screen renders. Providers are enabled and disabled through configuration without a redeploy; a disabled provider disappears from here and refuses both sign-in and registration.
get.summary: List the identity providers currently accepting sign-in

post.description: Builds the authorization redirect for the provider. The caller sends the browser to `authorizationUrl` and must hold `state`, `nonce` and `codeVerifier` server-side across the redirect — they bind the callback to this challenge and are required to complete it.

400.description: The redirect URI is not within the provider’s registered redirect configuration (problem type social-redirect-rejected).

403.description: The provider is not available for sign-in (problem type social-provider-unavailable). Identical for a provider that is disabled and one that is not registered.

post.summary: Begin a provider sign-in

post.description: Redeems the authorization code, validates the identity assertion, and issues the same session shape as password sign-in — matching on the provider’s stable subject identifier, never on the email address. A first-time identity registers when the flow began as registration; a sign-in that matches nothing is answered distinctly so registration can be offered instead.

401.description: The exchange failed (problem type social-exchange-failed), or the identity is linked to no account and the flow began as sign-in — see 404.

403.description: The provider is unavailable (problem type social-provider-unavailable), or the account awaits email verification (problem type email-unverified) — for a fresh registration whose provider did not assert the address verified, the account exists and the verification email is on its way when this answers.

404.description: The authenticated identity is linked to no account (problem type social-identity-unknown). Nothing was created; the caller offers registration.

409.description: The asserted address already has an account (problem type social-email-in-use). A provider assertion alone never attaches to an existing account; the resolution is password sign-in.

429.description: Too many completion attempts from this address in the window.

post.summary: Complete a provider sign-in

get.description: What S-28 lists. The provider’s subject identifier is deliberately not included: it is the provider’s own identifier for a person and no screen has a use for it.

200.description: The linked providers, ordered by provider.

get.summary: The providers linked to the signed-in account

post.description: Redeems the authorization code and attaches what the provider asserts (UC-11). Requires the current password: a link adds a way in, so a stolen session must not be able to attach one and outlive the password change its owner would reach for. **The asserted address need not match the account’s** — a personal provider account is routinely not a work address, and BR-ID-3 is satisfied by the re-authentication, never by comparing emails.

403.description: The current password did not match (problem type credential-invalid).

409.description: That provider identity is already attached to an account, or this account already holds one for this provider. Deliberately one answer for both — the other would name a stranger’s account.

429.description: Too many re-authentication attempts for this account in the window (§12.5.6).

post.summary: Link a provider identity to the signed-in account

post.description: Removes the identity (UC-12), unless it is the account’s **last remaining credential** — BR-ID-4, counted across the password and every linked provider rather than assumed. An account with no usable credential is unrecoverable and takes its organization memberships with it, so the refusal names the way out: set a password first.

204.description: The provider is no longer linked.

403.description: The current password did not match (problem type credential-invalid).

409.description: The account holds no identity for that provider, or removing it would leave no credential at all (BR-ID-4).

post.summary: Unlink a provider identity

get.description: Answers "who can see our ESG data": every active member with their role, status and last activity. Unpaginated by design — the collection is bounded by the plan’s seat entitlement. Pending invitations are a separate resource and do not appear here.

403.description: The caller holds no membership in an active organization (problem type membership-required), or holds one in a role that is not organization_administrator (problem type insufficient-role).

get.summary: List everyone with access to the active organization

patch.description: Takes effect on that member’s next request rather than at their next login, because the role is read from the membership record per request and is never carried in a token. Granting organization_administrator is how a second administrator is created, which is what makes demoting or removing the first one permissible.

404.description: No active member of this organization has that membership id.

409.description: The change would leave the organization with no Organization Administrator (problem type last-administrator). Promote another member first.

patch.summary: Change a member’s role, or promote them to Organization Administrator

delete.description: Ends access without deleting the account or the member’s attributed history: their contributions remain attributed in the change history, and the membership record is retained showing when access was granted and withdrawn. Their sessions are not ended — the next request they make is simply refused, and they keep access to any other organization they belong to.

404.description: No active member of this organization has that membership id.

409.description: Removing this member would leave the organization with no Organization Administrator (problem type last-administrator). Promote another member first.

delete.summary: Remove a member’s access to the organization

get.description: Every organization the caller is an active member of, with the role held in each, the organization’s name for display, and which one this request is acting for. An empty list is a normal answer — a verified account holds no membership until it creates an organization or accepts an invitation — and it is what sends a new user to create their first one. A list in which no entry is active is also normal: it is an account holding several memberships that has stated no preference, and it is what the organization switcher exists to resolve.

200.description: The caller’s memberships, ordered by organization name.

get.summary: List the organizations the signed-in account belongs to

get.description: The other half of "who can see our ESG data": people invited but not yet joined. Unpaginated by design — the collection is bounded by the plan’s seat entitlement. An invitation whose link has lapsed still appears, because it is what holds the invited address; resending it restores a working link.

403.description: The caller holds no membership in an active organization (problem type membership-required), or holds one in a role that is not organization_administrator (problem type insufficient-role).

get.summary: List the active organization’s outstanding invitations

post.description: Issues a single-use invitation bound to the address and emails it. The link lasts seven days and can be reissued or withdrawn at any time before it is accepted.

201.description: The invitation was issued and its email was queued.

400.description: The address is malformed, or the role is not one that can be invited.

409.description: The address already belongs to a member of this organization (problem type already-member), or an invitation to it is already outstanding (problem type invitation-outstanding) — resend or revoke that one instead. Two problem types rather than one, because the two have different resolutions and a client should not have to read the wording to tell them apart.

post.summary: Invite someone to the organization with an edit or view-only role

post.description: Reissues the link and restarts the seven days on the same invitation, so the person keeps their place in the list and their assigned role. The previously sent link stops working immediately — there is never more than one live link per invitation. An invitation whose link has already lapsed can be resent, which is what makes a forgotten one recoverable.

204.description: A fresh link was issued and its email was queued.

404.description: No outstanding invitation of this organization has that id — it was accepted or revoked.

post.summary: Send the invitation again

delete.description: The link stops working immediately, and the invited address is free to be invited again — at a different role, which is the usual reason. The record of the invitation is kept, so the history of who was offered access to the organization stays complete.

404.description: No outstanding invitation of this organization has that id. An invitation that has already been accepted is a membership; end that person’s access from the members collection.

post.description: What the invitation offers, so the recipient can decide whether to create an account. Consumes nothing: the link is spent by an explicit acceptance, never by being opened, so a mail scanner following it cannot burn someone’s invitation. A link that is spent, withdrawn or out of date answers why and withholds the rest.

200.description: The invitation’s standing, with its details where it is still usable.

post.summary: Read an invitation without using it

post.description: Grants the invited role in that organization and makes it the active one for this session, so the next request is already scoped to it. The invitation is single-use and is spent here. Someone who already has access keeps the role they hold — accepting never changes an existing role — and someone whose access was withdrawn earlier has it restored.

201.description: The organization joined, the role now held, and which of the three happened.

403.description: The request carries no session (problem type authentication-required), or is signed in as an account the invitation does not name (problem type invitation-address-mismatch). An invitation binds to one address, which is what stops a sign-in for a different one using it.

410.description: The link cannot be used (problem type invitation-not-acceptable). The document carries a standing member saying which: expired, consumed, revoked, or unknown. None is retryable — ask an administrator for a new invitation.

post.summary: Join the organization the invitation names

post.description: FR-13 and D-1: the creating user is granted the organization_administrator role by the act of creating, in the same transaction — an organization committed without its founding membership would be unreachable by everyone including its creator. The caller keeps every membership they already held, and the new organization becomes the calling session’s active one, so the response is the organization the next request will be scoped to. That is not a convenience: an account holding two memberships with no stated preference has no active organization at all, so founding a second without pointing the session would refuse the caller access to the one they were already using.

201.description: The organization as created. Profile fields S-04 does not collect are null.

400.description: The country registers no legal-form vocabulary, so the platform does not operate there yet (problem type country-not-supported). No edit to the request will change the answer — GET /organizations/legal-forms lists the countries this route accepts.

post.summary: Create an organization and become its Organization Administrator

get.description: Configuration, not code (AD-4): the set moves without a redeploy and propagates within five seconds. S-04 builds its country field from the entries and S-15 its legal-form field from the matching one, which is why both are answered in a single request. The values are keys — resolve them to labels through the message catalogue.

200.description: One entry per country the platform operates in. A list of one at MVP.

get.summary: The countries an organization may be created in, and each one’s legal forms

get.description: FR-15’s legal identity, which propagates into every report the organization produces. Distinct from the billing account (FR-106): the invoiced legal person is not always the reporting entity, particularly in a group structure.

403.description: The caller holds no membership in an active organization (problem type membership-required), or holds one in a role that is not organization_administrator (problem type insufficient-role).

get.summary: The active organization’s profile

patch.description: A patch: a field absent from the body is unchanged, and an explicit null clears it. Every change is attributed and timestamped by the database itself (FR-15), so the change history names the acting user and the field that moved without this route recording anything.

200.description: The organization as it stands after the change.

400.description: The submitted legal form is not registered for the organization’s country (problem type legal-form-unknown) — reachable by changing the country as well as by changing the form — or the submitted country registers no vocabulary at all (problem type country-not-supported).

get.description: Archived entities are included and carry their status — S-13 filters them out of active selection, and the collection publishes what exists so a reader can find one deliberately.
get.summary: The organization’s reporting entities

post.description: An organization may hold several: most SMEs hold exactly one and the model does not assume it (FR-17). Sites may be supplied now or added later.

400.description: An activity code the organization’s country does not register (problem type nace-code-unknown). The classifier is CAEM Rev.2 for Moldova, 1:1 with NACE Rev.2.

post.summary: Create a reporting entity

get.description: FR-17’s NACE code(s), offered rather than only validated. The classifier is CAEM Rev.2 for Moldova, 1:1 with NACE Rev.2, and it is configuration (AD-4) — so the set moves without a redeploy. **This searches server-side and answers a bounded page**: the classifier is 996 entries across three languages, and shipping it to a browser to filter there is a payload no screen budget admits. The query matches a code by its digits — 10.71, 1071 and 10 71 are one query — and a label without regard to case or diacritics, because a reader types brutarie for brutărie. An empty query answers an empty list rather than an arbitrary slice of the classifier. Labels arrive in the request’s negotiated language.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most 50; values outside the range are clamped rather than refused.

parameters.name: codes
parameters.description: Comma-separated codes a record already holds, resolved to their words in the negotiated language. Takes precedence over q, matches exactly rather than by prefix, answers in the order given, and drops a code the classifier no longer carries rather than inventing a label for it.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What the reader typed. Empty answers nothing.

200.description: Matching codes, code matches before label matches, each in classifier order.

get.summary: Search the activity classifier registered for the organization’s country

404.description: No entity of the active organization has that id — including when it is another tenant’s.

get.summary: One reporting entity, with its sites

patch.description: A patch: a field absent is unchanged. Sending `sites` saves the whole collection. A report for a closed period keeps the values in force when it was prepared (FR-18), so an edit here is not retroactive — S-13 states that consequence before the save.

400.description: A consolidated basis with nothing inside the boundary (problem type consolidation-boundary-empty), or an unregistered activity code (nace-code-unknown).

409.description: The entity is archived, so its master data is read-only (problem type entity-archived). It stays readable — its historical reports and exports must remain retrievable.

patch.summary: Edit a reporting entity’s master data

post.description: Removes it from active selection and retains its historical reports and exports intact (FR-20, UC-55) — the entity is sold, merged or dissolved, and prior filings must stay retrievable. An action-noun route rather than DELETE, because nothing is deleted.

409.description: The entity is already archived (problem type entity-archived).

post.summary: Archive a reporting entity

get.description: Scoped to one entity because a period only means anything against one (FR-21). The active organization comes from the session, never from a parameter.
get.summary: List the reporting periods of one entity, newest first

post.description: The template and taxonomy versions are pinned by the system from the registered adoption (FR-66, DR-4) and the preceding period is linked automatically (FR-45) — neither is a field on this request, deliberately.

400.description: The dates do not describe a period.

404.description: No such entity in the active organization.

409.description: The entity is archived, another period overlaps these dates, or no taxonomy version is registered to pin.

post.summary: Open a reporting period (UC-56)

404.description: No such period in the active organization.

get.summary: One reporting period, with its pinned versions

patch.description: The pinned versions are not editable: DR-4 moves them only by an explicit migration run (FR-69), so no field on this request can name one.

200.description: The period as it now stands.

400.description: The dates do not describe a period.

404.description: No such period in the active organization.

409.description: Another period overlaps these dates, or the period is locked.

get.description: UX-72 requires an amendment to look like an amendment, so this is a read every member has — a Contributor working in a reopened period must be able to see that it was reopened and why, not only the administrator who reopened it.

404.description: No such period in the active organization.

get.summary: Every reopening of this period, most recent first (UC-58)

post.description: A locked period takes no writes from anyone, the administrator included — reopening is the only route through it (FR-22). An irreversible-class action under UX-71, which is why it is a named route rather than a field on the patch above.

404.description: No such period in the active organization.

409.description: The period is already locked.

post.summary: Lock the period (UC-57)

post.description: The reason is required and is displayed on the period thereafter (UX-72) — an amendment must look like an amendment. The acting user and the timestamp are recorded by the system and are not fields on this request.

404.description: No such period in the active organization.

409.description: The period is not locked.

post.summary: Reopen the period, recording who, when and why (UC-58)

get.description: Organization-wide by default, which is what FR-23’s overview reads. Narrowed to one entity by query parameter — the active organization comes from the session, never from a parameter.
get.summary: List the reports in the active organization, newest reporting period first (UC-17)

post.description: The template and taxonomy versions are copied from the period, which pinned them when it was opened (FR-66, DR-4) — neither is a field on this request, deliberately. A period carries at most one report.

404.description: No such reporting period in the active organization.

409.description: The period already has a report, or the period is locked.

post.summary: Create the report for a reporting period (UC-18)

404.description: No such report in the active organization.

get.summary: One report, with its pinned versions

patch.description: Comprehensive may be added to a report already in progress. The pinned versions are not editable: DR-4 moves them only by an explicit migration run (FR-69), so no field on this request can name one and the application role holds no privilege to write one.

200.description: The report as it now stands.

404.description: No such report in the active organization.

409.description: The reporting period is locked.

get.description: S-07's persistent module list (UX-5). Resolved from the report's OWN pinned taxonomy version, never the newest registered (DR-4).

200.description: The modules the pinned version carries, in the standard's order.

404.description: No such report in the active organization.

get.summary: The report's modules, with how much of each is answered

get.description: Taxonomy shape, resolved label with its standing (NFR-24), and the stored value, joined server-side because only this tier holds all three.

404.description: No such report in the active organization.

get.summary: One wizard step: the module's fields, with their values

put.description: FR-37 persists on blur or step change, so this takes one value or a queue flush. An upsert on the natural key, so FR-38's retry writes the same row rather than a second one. Refused while the report's period is locked (FR-22), by the database as well as by the use case.

200.description: What was durably committed — UX-36 acknowledges the commit, not local state.

400.description: A field the pinned version does not name.

404.description: No such report in the active organization.

409.description: The reporting period is locked (FR-22).

put.summary: Persist one or more field values (autosave)

get.description: Resolves the prior period from the linkage rather than from the caller (FR-45), and answers each value with whether it is comparable across the two pinned taxonomy versions (FR-46). Where there is no comparative, `availability` says which of the two reasons applies.

200.description: The prior period’s answers, each with its comparability verdict.

404.description: No such report in the active organization.

get.summary: The prior period’s answers for this report

post.description: UC-68 step one. Verifies email and password; on success the sealed, five-minute factor challenge rides an httpOnly cookie and the body names whose code is now awaited. Failures are uniform for unknown and deactivated operators alike, throttled per address, and locked after repeated failure.

201.description: The credential held; the factor challenge is open and rides the cookie.

401.description: The email address or the password is not right — one answer for both (problem type credential-invalid).

403.description: The operator account is locked after repeated failures (problem type admin-account-locked; released by another administrator or the provisioning CLI).

429.description: Too many attempts for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Verify the elevated credential and open the second-factor challenge

post.description: UC-68 step two. Judges the TOTP code against the challenge cookie step one set; on success the session is established as a sealed httpOnly cookie and the challenge is cleared — no token appears in the body (FR-75: the factor is mandatory, without exception).

201.description: The session was established; the cookie carries it.

401.description: No open challenge, or it lapsed (problem type authentication-required — sign-in restarts from the credential); or the code is wrong (problem type factor-invalid, disclosed only past the credential bar — the challenge stays open for a retype).

403.description: The operator account is locked (problem type admin-account-locked) — a wrong code counts toward the same threshold as a wrong password.

429.description: Too many attempts for this address in the window. Identical either way.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with the second factor

get.description: The console router’s probe. Judges the sealed cookie: a live access token answers directly; an expired one is rotated server-side and the successor cookie set on this response. 401 means sign in again.

200.description: The current session, rotated if its access token had expired.

401.description: No usable session (problem type authentication-required), or its lifetimes ran out (problem type session-expired).

get.summary: Read the current administrative session

delete.description: Revokes the session server-side and clears the cookies — any half-open factor challenge included. Idempotent, and identical for cookies that were never real — signing out is not an endpoint that confirms anything.

204.description: The session is terminated, or already was.

delete.summary: Sign out of the administrative realm

info.title: easyesg API
info.description: One versioned REST surface. Both front ends are ordinary clients of it and no privileged route exists (DR-11, NFR-16). The active organization comes from the session — never from a header, a path segment or a token claim.

status.description: No application data is reachable while an account is unverified (FR-1). An unverified account expires 7 days after registration.

verifiedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. Null while the account is unverified.

email.description: Case is preserved as supplied; uniqueness is case-insensitive.

password.description: Minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character. Letters are matched by Unicode property, so Romanian and Russian letters count as letters.

invitationToken.description: An organization invitation being acted on. When it is still usable and was sent to this same address, the account is created already confirmed and no confirmation email is sent — the invitation link is itself proof the address was reached. Anything else is ignored and registration proceeds normally.

token.description: The value from the verification link. Single-use and valid for 24 hours from issue.

email.description: Malformed addresses are refused as requests; well-formed ones are never.

token.description: The single-use value from the reset link.

password.description: The replacement password, under the same policy as registration: minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character.

enrolled.description: Whether a confirmed second factor is in force on this account.

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: Unspent recovery codes. Zero with an enrolled factor is a real state, not an error — the user has spent them all and should re-issue before they need one.

secret.description: The base32 secret, for an authenticator that is being configured by hand rather than by scanning. Shown once and never returned again.

enrolmentUri.description: The same secret in the Key Uri Format an authenticator’s QR scanner consumes, emitted by the same object that verifies the code, so a client cannot configure parameters the server will not accept.

password.description: The account’s current password. Required for every account that has one; omitted only by an account that signs in through a provider and holds no password.

recoveryCodes.description: Single-use codes, shown exactly once. Re-issuing replaces the whole set, so any code from a previous set stops working the moment a new one is issued.

code.description: The current code shown by the authenticator app, which is what proves the secret was captured. Enrolment activates on this and not before.

otherSessionsTerminated.description: How many other sessions were ended. Always 0 when the election was not made, and 0 is a normal answer when it was — the account simply had no other device signed in.

currentPassword.description: The password in force now. A change without the correct one is refused (FR-7).

password.description: The replacement, under the same policy as registration: minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character.

terminateOtherSessions.description: End the account’s **other** active sessions. Opt-in, because FR-7 says *where the user elects it* — and the session making this request is never one of them, so the device the change was made from keeps working.

locale.description: The interface language persisted on the account (FR-10).

kind.description: The discriminator sign-in answers with. `challenged` is the other member, and carries a factor challenge instead of a session (UC-194).

accessToken.description: Bearer token for the Authorization header. Signed, short-lived; carries the session identity and no authorization data.

accessTokenExpiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. At most 15 minutes after issuance.

refreshToken.description: Opaque, single-use. Present it to the refresh endpoint to obtain a successor pair; it is invalidated by that refresh, by sign-out, and by a consumed password reset.

refreshTokenExpiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When this session dies if never refreshed again — the earlier of its idle and absolute bounds.

kind.description: The discriminator. `signed_in` carries a session; this one carries a challenge, and a client must branch on it rather than probing for a field.

challenge.description: Opaque and sealed — it proves only that this API verified this account’s password just now, and it is not a session and cannot become one. Present it back with the code. The client stores it; where is the client’s decision (the web tier keeps it in a short-lived httpOnly cookie, as it does the OAuth transaction).

expiresAt.description: When the challenge stops being accepted — epoch milliseconds, UTC (OQ-50). Stated rather than left for the client to infer, so a screen can say how long is left without knowing the policy.

password.description: Verified against the stored credential; failures are uniform and rate-limited.

challenge.description: The opaque challenge returned by the first step. Sealed; the API is the only thing that can read it.

code.description: A current code from the authenticator, or one of the account’s recovery codes. The two are distinguishable by shape, so one field serves both.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token exactly as issued. Single-use: a successful refresh replaces it, and the replaced value is rejected from then on.
The refresh token of the session to terminate. Possession is the authentication: it is what the web tier actually holds, and it keeps sign-out working after the access token has already expired.

providers.description: Providers currently accepting sign-in and registration.

authorizationUrl.description: The provider's authorization endpoint with this flow's parameters applied.

state.description: Binds the callback to this challenge. Compare against the callback query.

nonce.description: Required by the completion endpoint; validated against the ID token.

codeVerifier.description: The PKCE verifier the completion endpoint presents to the token endpoint.

redirectUri.description: Where the provider returns the browser. Must match the redirect configuration registered for the provider exactly.

code.description: The authorization code from the provider's callback.

state.description: The state the challenge issued, as returned by the callback.

codeVerifier.description: The PKCE verifier the challenge issued.

redirectUri.description: The redirect URI the flow began with — must match the challenge exactly.

intent.description: What the user was doing when the flow began. A sign-in that matches no account is offered registration rather than silently given one; a registration that matches an existing address is refused rather than linked.

assertedEmail.description: The address the provider asserted at the last sign-in. Deliberately allowed to differ from the account’s own — it is a recorded fact, not an identity — and it is what tells a user which of their provider accounts this is.

code.description: The authorization code returned by the provider.

state.description: The `state` from the sealed transaction, echoed by the provider.

nonce.description: The `nonce` from the sealed transaction, checked in the ID token.

codeVerifier.description: The PKCE verifier from the sealed transaction.

redirectUri.description: The redirect URI the code was issued against — checked against the allowlist.

password.description: The account’s current password. Required for every account that has one — a link adds a way in, so a stolen session must not be able to attach a provider (§12.5.6). Omitted only by an account that signs in through a provider and holds no password.
The account’s current password, on the same rule as linking: an attacker on a stolen session must not be able to strip the owner’s other provider.

id.description: Identifies this membership for a role change or a removal.

status.description: Always active in this list: a removed membership is history rather than access. Pending invitations are a separate resource and are not members.

lastActiveAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the last request this member made against the organization, or null if they have not returned since being granted access.

joinedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when access was granted.

role.description: The role to grant. Setting the role a member already holds is permitted and changes nothing. Granting organization_administrator is how a second administrator is created.

organizationId.description: The organization the caller belongs to.

organizationName.description: Shown in the organization switcher and on the home screen.

role.description: The role held in THIS organization. It may differ in each of them.

joinedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when access was granted.

active.description: Whether this request is acting for this organization. Exactly one membership carries it once a preference is settled; **none does** while the caller holds several and has stated no preference, which is a normal state and the one the organization switcher resolves. It is resolved per request from the session and is never a property of the membership row.

id.description: Identifies this invitation for a resend or a revocation.

email.description: The address the invitation is bound to.

issuedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the most recent issue or resend. A resend moves this, because it reissues the link rather than re-delivering it.

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds after which the link no longer works. A lapsed invitation still appears here — it is what holds the address, and resending it restores a working link.

email.description: The address to invite. The invitation binds to it: acceptance is refused for any other address, including one a social provider asserts.

role.description: The role acceptance grants. Organization Administrator is not invitable — it is granted to an existing member instead.

standing.description: Whether the link can still be used, and if not, why. The three unusable values are separate because each has its own resolution and its own sentence on screen.

organizationName.description: The organization doing the inviting. Null unless the link is usable.

invitedEmail.description: The address the invitation is bound to — acceptance is refused for any other, including one a social provider asserts. Null unless the link is usable.

role.description: The role acceptance grants. Null unless the link is usable.

token.description: The single-use token from the invitation email. Sent in the body rather than the URL so it stays out of access logs and referrer headers.

organizationId.description: The organization just joined, now the active one.

organizationName.description: Its name, for the confirmation the screen shows.

role.description: The role the account now holds. For someone who was already a member this is their existing role — accepting an invitation never changes it.

grant.description: What the acceptance did: created a new membership, restored one that had been withdrawn, or found that access already stood.

accountId.description: The acting account, or null where the change was not made by one.

email.description: The acting account’s address, for display. Null where that account no longer exists — the trail deliberately carries no foreign key, so an attribution outlives the account it names (NFR-28). There is no display name to show instead: registration collects none.

at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the change.

legalForm.description: A key from the vocabulary registered for countryCode, or null where none is recorded yet — S-04 does not collect it. Resolve it to a label through the message catalogue; it is never a sentence.

idno.description: FR-16’s primary identifier, or null until S-15 records it — S-04 collects none.

lei.description: The Legal Entity Identifier, or null. Optional by OQ-18: few Moldovan SMEs hold one, and it is kept so B1 stays conformant for the readers who require it.

contactEmail.description: How the PLATFORM reaches this organization. Distinct from reportContactEmail, which is printed on the report cover for its readers.

reportContactName.description: FR-15’s report-cover contact — the person a reader of the published report contacts about its content. A second contact rather than a rename of contactEmail: in an SME the account administrator and the person who answers a question about a figure in B3 are routinely different people. Collected on S-15 only; S-04 sets neither.

lastChange.description: Who last changed any field of this record, and when (FR-15). Read from the per-field audit trail the database writes, not from a column the application maintains. Null where the trail holds nothing for this record — an unusual state, and a real answer rather than an error.

createdAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the organization was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the last profile change.

name.description: The registered legal name (FR-15). Propagates into every report the organization produces.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, case-insensitive and stored upper case. It is not merely an address line: it selects the legal-form vocabulary, so a country the platform does not yet register one for is refused with problem type country-not-supported. GET /organizations/legal-forms is the list of countries this accepts.

contactEmail.description: Where the platform writes to about this organization. Distinct from the billing contact (FR-106).

contactPhone.description: Free-form, deliberately unvalidated beyond its length — there is no international format this could enforce without refusing real numbers.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case. An organization may be created in this country.

legalForms.description: Legal-form keys, in the order they are registered. Each resolves to a label through the message catalogue (OQ-43), so a form registered ahead of its wording renders its key.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Changing it re-checks the stored legal form against the new country’s vocabulary, so a move that would strand the form is refused with problem type legal-form-unknown rather than silently leaving a value no list contains.

legalForm.description: A key from the vocabulary registered for the organization’s country — see GET /organizations/legal-forms. Null clears it, which is always permitted: an organization that has not decided is a state S-15 must be able to return to.

idno.description: FR-16’s primary identifier — Moldova’s thirteen-digit state identification number. Its shape is validated on entry; the thirteenth digit is a check digit whose algorithm is not published in the defining instrument, so it is not yet verified. Null clears it.

lei.description: FR-16’s optional additional identifier — the Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), upper case. Both its shape and its ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 check digits are verified, and the two refuse with different problem types because they have different resolutions. Null clears it.

reportContactName.description: FR-15’s report-cover contact — the person a reader of the published report contacts about its content, printed on the cover. A second contact rather than a rename of contactEmail, which is how the platform reaches the organization. Null clears it.

status.description: Archived entities leave active selection and keep their reports and exports (FR-20). They remain readable here; their master data is read-only.

archivedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, or null while active.

consolidationBasis.description: Null until stated. B1 discloses it and task 38’s calculator aggregates over it.

consolidationMembers.description: The boundary’s subsidiaries. Meaningful when the basis is `consolidated`; kept regardless.

code.description: CAEM Rev.2, 1:1 with NACE Rev.2 to four characters. Sections are one character, divisions two, groups four and classes five including the dot.

label.description: The activity’s name in the request’s negotiated language, falling back to a language the classifier does carry rather than hiding the entry.

id.description: Omit to add a site; supply an existing id to edit that one. A site the array omits is removed, which is what makes this collection a save rather than an append.

latitude.description: Decimal degrees as a string, not a number. B5’s biodiversity applicability is evaluated from these coordinates (BR-APP-3), so a value that drifts in the last places is a determination that changes — which is why neither the column nor the wire uses a float.

id.description: Omit to add; supply an id to edit that member.

name.description: The subsidiary’s legal name, as B1 publishes it.

legalForm.description: A key from the country’s legal-form vocabulary.

naceCodes.description: CAEM Rev.2 codes — 1:1 with NACE Rev.2 to four characters, which is what B1 exports. Each is admitted against the classifier registered for the organization’s country; an empty array means the entity is not classified yet, which FR-17 permits.

sites.description: The entity’s sites, as a whole collection. Omit to leave them alone; send an array to save them — members with an id are edited, members without are added, and stored sites the array omits are removed.

consolidationBasis.description: FR-19’s reporting boundary, which bounds every quantitative figure in the report and which B1 discloses. Null until stated — VSME asks the question explicitly, so there is no default answering it on the undertaking’s behalf. Setting `consolidated` requires at least one subsidiary inside the boundary.

consolidationMembers.description: The subsidiaries inside the boundary, as a whole collection — the same save semantics as `sites`. Recorded whatever the basis says: switching to `individual` leaves the list standing, and B1 reads it only when the basis is `consolidated`.

name.description: The entity’s name, as it is reported on.

legalForm.description: A key from the country’s legal-form vocabulary.

naceCodes.description: CAEM Rev.2 codes — 1:1 with NACE Rev.2 to four characters, which is what B1 exports. Each is admitted against the classifier registered for the organization’s country; an empty array means the entity is not classified yet, which FR-17 permits.

sites.description: The entity’s sites, as a whole collection. Omit to leave them alone; send an array to save them — members with an id are edited, members without are added, and stored sites the array omits are removed.

consolidationBasis.description: FR-19’s reporting boundary, which bounds every quantitative figure in the report and which B1 discloses. Null until stated — VSME asks the question explicitly, so there is no default answering it on the undertaking’s behalf. Setting `consolidated` requires at least one subsidiary inside the boundary.

consolidationMembers.description: The subsidiaries inside the boundary, as a whole collection — the same save semantics as `sites`. Recorded whatever the basis says: switching to `individual` leaves the list standing, and B1 reads it only when the basis is `consolidated`.

date.description: ISO 8601 calendar date. No time, no offset.

timezone.description: IANA zone that determines the date. Admitted against the runtime tz database.

templateVersion.description: The EFRAG Digital Template release this period is pinned to (DR-4, FR-66).

taxonomyVersion.description: The VSME taxonomy release this period is pinned to (DR-4, FR-66).

priorPeriodId.description: The immediately preceding period for the same entity, from which comparatives resolve (FR-45). Null for an entity’s first period.

entitySnapshotId.description: The entity master data as it stood when this period was opened (FR-18).

lockedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. Non-null means the period is locked and takes no writes from anyone, including an administrator — reopening is the only route through it (FR-22).

lockedBy.description: The account that locked it. Retained after that account loses access or is removed (FR-55).

periodEnd.description: The last day IN the period, not the day after.

dueDate.description: When the report must be complete — a different fact from when the period ends, and what deadline notices count down to.

lockedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When the lock this reopening ended was placed.

reason.description: Why the period is being reopened. Displayed on the period thereafter (UX-72).

entityName.description: The undertaking’s name as it stands now — a wayfinding label. What a filing discloses comes from the period’s point-in-time snapshot instead (FR-18).

status.description: Where the report stands. Open and locked follow the reporting period’s lock, which is their only writer (FR-22).

templateVersion.description: The EFRAG Digital Template release this report is pinned to (DR-4, FR-66). Copied from the reporting period at creation and moved only by an explicit migration run (FR-69).

taxonomyVersion.description: The VSME taxonomy release this report is pinned to (DR-4, FR-66).

reportingPeriodId.description: The reporting period this report covers. A period carries at most one report, and the period is what determines the pinned versions (FR-66, DR-4).

scope.description: Which VSME modules this report covers. Comprehensive is additive over Basic and may also be added later (FR-177). Defaults to Basic.
FR-177: Comprehensive may be added to a report already in progress.

answered.description: Fields with a stored answer, including nil return and not available.

total.description: Fields the pinned version puts in this module.

lastAnsweredAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC — when the module's most recent answer was stored, or null where nothing in it is answered. Where work last happened is where a returning reporter resumes (FR-39).

value.description: The member's taxonomy-qualified name — what an answer stores; the Excel export maps it to the template's own value. An enumeration_set answer holds its chosen values space-separated.

label.description: The member's wording in the request's locale; null where the platform holds none — ISO 3166 members, whose names the client resolves from its own catalogue.

code.description: The classification's own code, where it has one.

dimensionKey.description: An axis member, or empty where the element is undimensioned.

ordinal.description: Position within a repeating group; 0 where there is none.

kind.description: Which of the typed columns this element answers into.

periodType.description: Reported FOR the period (duration) or AS AT a moment in it (instant). The two compare differently against the prior period.

axes.description: Axes this element is dimensioned along; empty for most.

order.description: EFRAG's own presentation order within the module.

label.description: Null where the pinned version carries no label for this element in this locale.

labelStanding.description: Whether the wording is EFRAG's own or platform-authored. Carried per field because it travels with the text — of three locales only English is official.

help.description: EFRAG's documentation label for the element, or null where the package carries none (UX-17).

options.description: The answers a choice field offers; null for every kind that is not an enumeration.

valueNumeric.description: Decimal as a string, never a float.

carriedForward.description: Carried forward from the prior period, and marked for review.

taxonomyVersion.description: The report's own pinned version, which is what these fields were resolved from.

dimensionKey.description: An axis member; omit for an undimensioned element.

valueNumeric.description: Decimal as a string, never a float (NFR-58).

notAvailableReason.description: Required exactly when the state is not available (FR-32) — enforced by the store.

carriedForward.description: FR-47: this value was carried forward from the prior period.

values.description: One field on blur, or everything a step change or an offline queue accumulated (FR-37, FR-38). The write is an upsert on the natural key, so a retried queue does not double-write.

fiscalYear.description: The fiscal year the comparative was reported for.

taxonomyVersion.description: The taxonomy version the prior report was authored under. Present because it may differ from the current report’s (DR-4), which is what `comparability` is about.

dimensionKey.description: An axis member, or empty where the element is undimensioned.

ordinal.description: Position within a repeating group; 0 where there is none.

valueNumeric.description: Decimal as a string, never a float.

comparability.description: Whether this value can be placed beside the current field. A fact read from the two pinned taxonomy versions, not a decision about what to render.

taxonomyVersion.description: The current report’s pinned taxonomy version.

availability.description: Why there is nothing to show, where there is nothing. A first year and a prior period nobody reported on are different situations for a reporter (FR-45).

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When the challenge lapses and sign-in restarts from the credential (§12.5.6 — five minutes).

password.description: Verified against the elevated credential; failures are uniform and throttled.

role.description: The platform-side actor (actors.md: PA or BO).

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC. When the session dies if never used again — the earlier of its idle (8 h) and absolute (12 h) bounds.

totpCode.description: The current TOTP code (FR-75 — the second factor is mandatory, without exception).
